section_summary: This section contains diplomatic reporting and internal State Department memoranda from late 1938 and early 1939 regarding political, military, and economic developments in Japan and Japanese-occupied China. It includes the concluding portion of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for August 1938, the full monthly report for September 1938 (Despatch No. 3308), a State Department review memorandum by Laurence E. Salisbury, and the opening portion of the monthly report for November 1938 (Despatch No. 3521). Major subjects covered include Japan's formal challenge to the Open Door doctrine in East Asia, restrictions on foreign trade and navigation along the Yangtze River, military campaigns around Hankow and Canton, Cabinet friction resulting in Foreign Minister Kazushige Ugaki's resignation, and tightening domestic economic mobilization.

subfiles.about: Continuation and concluding portion of the American Embassy in Tokyo's monthly report on conditions in Japan for August 1938, including schedules of despatches and telegrams sent to Washington.
subfiles.summary: This concluding section of the August 1938 monthly report discusses Japanese government finance, bond issuances for the China campaign, and general economic conditions under national mobilization. It reviews foreign trade statistics, agricultural typhoon damage, exchange stringency, gold shipments to the United States, and Japanese development companies in North and Central China. The document concludes with complete schedules of Embassy despatches (Nos. 3163–3227) and telegrams (Nos. 507–568) sent to the Department of State during August 1938.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of August, 1938 (Sections VI-X and Enclosures)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting the Tokyo Embassy's comprehensive monthly report on political, diplomatic, military, and economic conditions in Japan and China during September 1938.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 144 reviewing Japanese internal politics, international relations, military operations in China, and economic conditions during September 1938. Key diplomatic issues include American representations regarding Japanese naval attacks on commercial aircraft of the China National Aviation Corporation, the Mengchiang oil monopoly, navigation rights on the Yangtze River, consular interference at Chefoo, and the Hankow safety zone. The report also details Japan's reaction to the European crisis over Czechoslovakia, President Roosevelt's peace appeal, British and French friction with Japanese authorities, League of Nations sanctions proposals, Cabinet conflict culminating in Foreign Minister Kazushige Ugaki's resignation over the China affairs organ, and major typhoon damage in the Kwanto region. Complete schedules of despatches (Nos. 3228–3291) and telegrams (Nos. 569–636) sent during September 1938 are appended.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3308 Transmitting Report No. 144: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of September, 1938

subfiles.about: Internal Department of State charge slip recording the tracking and charging of document 894.00PR/131 to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs.

subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip for File 894.00PR/131

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing and analyzing the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for November 1938.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Laurence E. Salisbury of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs reviews Tokyo's November 1938 report for Political Adviser Stanley K. Hornbeck. The memorandum highlights Japan's note of November 19 asserting that former concepts and the Open Door no longer apply to East Asia, alongside conversations between Foreign Minister Arita, Counselor Dooman, and Ambassador Grew. It also notes unresolved protests regarding Yangtze navigation, the Japanese seizure of the Canton Maritime Customs, Japan's warning on the expansion of hostilities into western China, trade restrictions in North China, and domestic economic stagnation under the National General Mobilization Law.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Reviewing Tokyo's Monthly Report for November, 1938

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan during November 1938, covering pages 1 through 14 of Report No. 146.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 146 reviewing Japanese affairs for November 1938 (pages 1–14). The report focuses on the diplomatic confrontation regarding American rights in China following Japan's note of November 18, which claimed that traditional Open Door concepts were obsolete in the new East Asian situation, and details extensive conversations between Foreign Minister Hachiro Arita, Counselor Eugene H. Dooman, and Ambassador Grew. It further records American protests against the closed navigation on the Yangtze River, the Japanese seizure of the Chinese Maritime Customs at Canton, Japan's notification of expanding hostilities across western China (Shensi, Hupeh, Hunan, Suchow, Batang, Tali), and Japanese export embargoes on wool and hemp in North China.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3521 Transmitting Report No. 146: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of November 1938 (Pages 1-14)
